newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-HOSTILE DONALD SENDS SUSSEX CRASHING.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-HOSTILE DONALD SENDS SUSSEX CRASHING.

text.p: South African fast bowler Allan Donald captured four for 11 in 10.2 overs as Warwickshire routed Sussex for 63 in the English county championship on Friday.
Donald's hostile display on a quick and bouncy pitch at Edgbaston forced Sussex to follow on 164 behind, and they slumped to seven for two at the close on the second day of the four-day match.
The South African was well supported by medium pacers Graeme Welch and Dougie Brown, and some excellent fielding, as Sussex were shot out in under two hours.

Donald struck twice in his sixth over when he had Toby Peirce caught behind and then plucked out Bill Athey's off stump to start a collapse which saw Sussex lose seven wickets for 28 runs in 41 balls.
He returned to bowl tailenders Alex Edwards and James Kirtley and Warwickshire had no hesitation in enforcing the follow on.
Bad light allowed them to bowl only four overs in Sussex's second innings but that was long enough for Brown to trap Peirce lbw for a duck and for Donald to have Rajesh Rao caught behind.
Australian Stuart Law completed his highest score for Essex of 175 to put his adopted county in command against champions Leicestershire at Colchester.
Law extended his overnight score from 124 to 175, driving with awesome power as he made his total runs from 223 deliveries.
He put on 317 for the third wicket with England batsman Nasser Hussain, whose 128 contained 15 fours and one six.
They powered Essex to 533 for eight declared, then reduced Leicestershire to 18 for two at the close.
Durham left-arm seamer Simon Brown snapped up five for 58 against Derbyshire as 17 wickets fell on the second day at Chester-le-Street.
Brown helped to restrict Derbyshire's second innings to 176 all out, leaving Durham needing 257 to win.
Durham, bowled out for 174 in their first innings after former England seamer Phil DeFreitas too five for 37, struggled in their quest for victory and were 48 for three at the close.
Worcestershire middle order batsman David Leatherdale hit his first century of the season to push his team to an imposing 409 for seven against Kent at Worcester.
Leatherdale struck 120 not out, completing his half-century in 127 balls and then racing to his hundred in another 62 deliveries. His innings included 14 fours and a six.
